9-panel cinematic storyboard sheet derived from Image 1. Mix Wide, Medium, and Tight shots of the same scene. No borders between panels.

Layout: 3x3 grid (9 panels) in a 16:9 landscape image.

Scene: Bright social-first editorial lifestyle photograph, 16:9, of Scarlett Doyle (Image 2) wearing her pale kiosk uniform polo with the collar loose and the hem half-tucked into denim cutoff shorts, bare legs, rubber thongs, an elastic hair tie around her wrist and a ring of kiosk keys hooked on her belt loop, coral lipstick on her mouth. She is caught in the starting frame mid-breath, one hand braced on the sun-bleached timber counter ledge of a small beachfront kiosk, shoulders squared and weight shifting onto her front foot as if about to push off and run, chin turning to glance sharply off-camera to the right, jaw set, a faint amused half-smile just forming — pure potential energy, nothing yet in motion. The kiosk interior is cramped and real: a chest freezer lid propped open breathing cold vapour, skewers of frozen pineapple in a plastic tub beading with meltwater, a stack of paper napkins weighted by a smooth beach stone, coiled hose, chipped mint-green paint on the serving hatch frame, a physical wall clock with tactile hands above her shoulder, taped handwritten-free cardboard scraps and a scatter of dried sand across the concrete floor. Through the open hatch behind her, blown-out morning ocean light: a bright wedge of Bondi sand, blurred surf breaking in soft bokeh, distant swimmers and a headland reduced to pale haze. Hard clean directional sunlight rakes in through the hatch, throwing a crisp geometric shadow band across her forearm and the counter, whites crisp and slightly warm in the highlights, shadows lifted and airy, one coral accent popping against the neutral timber and white base. Shot handheld with subtle micro-shake on a 35mm lens at eye level, shallow depth of field holding her face and the counter edge sharp while the beach dissolves behind, natural film grain, true-to-life clean color grade, high-key and immediate.

Every panel is a shot of the same scene as Image 1 — keep the characters, wardrobe, lighting, color grade, and texture consistent across all panels.

No text, dialogue bubbles, scene numbers, or watermarks.

Reference images define identity — keep every referenced character, object, and location consistent with its reference image; never render a reference image itself as a separate panel or subject.
